# teensy-panel: jumper wires (generated by tools/gen_teensy_panel.py)

22 AWG solid core, purple sleeve, 1.5 mm OD. Routes are given as hole > waypoint > hole in the vertical view (row 1 at the top, column A on the left); x is mm from the centre line, r is the row. Cut length includes 10 mm for the two stripped ends.

Before wiring: bridge both rail jumpers (top end joins the two - rails, bottom end the two + rails). The right rails are fed from the Teensy by W01/W02; the left rails then come live through the jumpers.

In KiCad the wires are also drawn as 1 mm tracks on F.Cu along their routes (KiCad 9 has no wire object), and the breadboard strips and rails as 1.3 mm tracks on B.Cu, so the ratsnest and DRC understand the build. Two airwires remain on purpose: the two rail jumpers, bridged with solder. Ignore the clearance and co-located-hole DRC errors: they come from the breadboard holes shared by several footprints.

Lanes: x=-15.6/-17.2/-18.8/-20.4 run beside column A, x=-2.9/0/+2.9 run down the centre gap, x=+15.6/+17.2 run beside column J. Wires at the same lane are stacked: the display wires lie on the board, the encoder wires ride on top of them. W07 hops over the x=-17.2 lane at row 36; W13 hops over rows 35-38; W04 rides over rows 34-38 down column G.
